h1: Brighter Smile. Up to 8 Shades Whiter. One Appointment.
intro: Professional teeth whitening at Marshall H. Brown, DDS & Associates delivers dramatically brighter results in a single visit — safely, comfortably, and under expert dental supervision. No strips, no guesswork, no waiting weeks for results.

body: Not all teeth whitening is created equal. While drugstore strips may seem convenient, they cannot deliver the dramatic, fast, or lasting results of professional in-office treatment under Dr. Brown's expert supervision.

Professional whitening uses prescription-strength agents 3–10× more concentrated than over-the-counter products — delivering results in one hour that would take weeks of daily strip application to approximate.
bullets: Results in 1 hour — vs. 2–4 weeks with strips
Up to 8 shades whiter — vs. 1–3 shades typically with strips
Full gum protection and custom fit — strips offer neither
Supervised safety with Dr. Brown — results last 1–3 years vs. 3–6 months

body: Boost is a professional-strength, in-office whitening system that lifts stains far beyond what any over-the-counter product can reach. A carefully formulated whitening gel is applied directly to your teeth under Dr. Brown's supervision and left to work in short, controlled sessions — delivering dramatic results in roughly 45–60 minutes. You leave our Fort Worth office with a noticeably brighter smile the very same day.

Because the treatment is chemically activated rather than light-dependent, it whitens evenly across the whole tooth surface and is effective on the deeper, more stubborn discolouration that builds up from coffee, tea, red wine, tobacco, and simple ageing.
bullets: 45–60 minutes in a single office visit
Up to 8 shades whiter
Even, predictable whitening across every tooth
Effective on deep-set and stubborn staining
Includes a take-home touch-up kit
Results typically last 1–3 years with good maintenance

sections.h2: Custom Take-Home Trays — At-Home, On Your Schedule
body: For patients who prefer to whiten at home, our custom take-home whitening system provides professional-grade results at your own pace. Dr. Brown creates custom-fitted whitening trays — far superior to generic store-bought kits. Simply apply the professional whitening gel and wear the trays for the prescribed time over 1–2 weeks.

Not sure which option is right for you? During your consultation, Dr. Brown will assess your current tooth shade, discuss your goals, and recommend the best system for your needs and sensitivity level.
bullets: Whiten at home on your schedule
Custom-fitted trays for a perfect seal
Professional-strength gel included
Results in 1–2 weeks of nightly use
Reusable trays — refill gel as needed

sections.h2: What's Causing Your Teeth to Be Discolored?
body: Different types of staining respond differently to whitening. Dr. Brown will assess your specific situation and recommend the most effective approach.
bullets: Coffee & tea stains — surface stains from tannins respond very well to professional whitening (excellent results)
Red wine staining — deep pigment staining that builds over time; professional whitening significantly reduces it (excellent results)
Tobacco staining — deep, stubborn yellow/brown stains that respond very well to professional in-office whitening
Age-related darkening — teeth naturally darken as enamel thins; whitening reverses much of this effect (excellent results)
Tetracycline staining — dark grey or brown banding from antibiotic exposure; whitening may help but veneers are often a better solution
Fluorosis — white spots or brown marks from excessive fluoride during development; whitening can help surface staining, but a consultation is needed

sections.h2: What to Expect During Your Whitening Appointment
body: Your in-office whitening appointment is relaxing, comfortable, and produces visible results before you leave our Fort Worth office.
bullets: Pre-treatment check — Dr. Brown examines your teeth and gums to confirm you're a good candidate; a cleaning first is recommended for maximum whitening penetration
Gum protection — a protective barrier gel is carefully applied to your gum tissue to shield it from the whitening agent
Whitening treatment — professional Boost gel is applied and left to work in 3–4 controlled sessions of about 15 minutes each
Reveal your smile — gel is rinsed away; most patients achieve 4–8 shades whiter, and you receive aftercare instructions and a touch-up kit

sections.h2: How to Make Your Whitening Results Last
body: With simple habits and a little mindfulness, your professional whitening results can remain bright and beautiful for 1–3 years. Here's Dr. Brown's aftercare guidance:

Tooth sensitivity after whitening? This is completely normal and temporary — resolving within 24–48 hours. Sensitivity toothpaste and avoiding very hot or cold foods during this period will help considerably.
bullets: Avoid staining foods for 48 hours after treatment — no coffee, red wine, tea, cola, or strongly pigmented foods immediately after whitening
Use a whitening toothpaste to maintain results between professional treatments
Drink staining beverages through a straw to minimise contact with your teeth
Brush and floss daily to prevent surface stain build-up
Schedule touch-up whitening every 12–18 months to keep your smile at peak brightness
Attend regular dental checkups — cleanings remove surface stains before they embed deeper

faqs.q: How much whiter will my teeth get?
faqs.a: Most patients achieve 4–8 shades whiter teeth with a single in-office Boost treatment. Results vary with the nature, depth, and severity of the staining. Yellow stains from coffee, tea, wine, and ageing respond particularly well. During your consultation, Dr. Brown will assess your current shade and give you a realistic expectation of what is achievable for your teeth.

faqs.q: How long do professional whitening results last?
faqs.a: Professional whitening results typically last 1–3 years depending on your dietary habits, oral hygiene routine, and lifestyle factors such as smoking. Patients who consume less coffee, tea, and red wine, and who maintain good daily brushing and flossing habits, tend to enjoy longer-lasting results. Touch-up whitening treatments — either in-office or with take-home trays — can be done every 12–18 months to keep your smile at peak brightness.

faqs.q: Should I choose in-office Boost whitening or take-home trays?
faqs.a: It depends on your timeline and how much control you want. In-office Boost is the fastest route — one appointment, maximum strength, and you see the result before you leave. Custom take-home trays work more gradually over one to two weeks, at a lower concentration, which some patients with sensitive teeth prefer. Many people do both: an in-office Boost treatment for the initial change, then trays to maintain it. Dr. Brown will recommend the right approach after looking at your staining and sensitivity.

faqs.q: Is teeth whitening safe for my enamel?
faqs.a: Yes. Professional teeth whitening performed under dental supervision is clinically proven to be safe and does not damage enamel when used as directed. The professional-strength agents used in Boost are formulated to be effective while protecting tooth structure. Some patients notice mild, temporary tooth or gum sensitivity for 24–48 hours afterwards — a normal response that resolves on its own. Over-the-counter products used excessively without supervision can cause enamel erosion, which is why dentist-administered whitening is both the safer and the more effective choice.

faqs.q: Who is a good candidate for teeth whitening?
faqs.a: Most adults with healthy teeth and gums are excellent candidates for professional whitening. The best candidates have yellow or brown surface staining from food, beverages, or tobacco; age-related tooth darkening; no active cavities or gum disease (these should be treated first); and healthy tooth enamel with no significant sensitivity issues. Whitening is less effective on intrinsic staining caused by tetracycline antibiotics or fluorosis — for these cases, Dr. Brown may recommend porcelain veneers as a more comprehensive solution.

faqs.q: Will whitening work on crowns, veneers, or fillings?
faqs.a: No — professional whitening agents only work on natural tooth enamel. They will not change the color of crowns, porcelain veneers, composite fillings, or dental bonding. If you have visible restorations and want a uniformly brighter smile, Dr. Brown will discuss your options — which may include replacing older restorations to match your newly whitened natural teeth, or discussing veneers as a comprehensive aesthetic solution.
